proposals.evidence: Previously reviewed comparative evidence: CDIAL 1268 gives Pali/Prakrit amba, Hindi ām/ā̃b, Old Awadhi āṁba and Gujarati ā̃b/ām. Retained mb and its simplification both belong to the mango family. Final vowels accord with the western forms. Updated disposition under the user’s explicit cross-Indo-Aryan policy: link this supported etymon despite unresolved inheritance versus intra-Indo-Aryan borrowing. The reflex edge records etymological family affiliation provisionally; it does not establish uninterrupted inheritance or an immediate donor. Prior hold: The mango family is clear, but the northwestern distribution may involve a regional loan; immediate donor not established.

proposals.evidence: Previously reviewed comparative evidence: The first branch of *kadala/kadalī* has Prakrit *kēla*, Hindi *kelā*, Bhojpuri *kerā* and Gujarati/Marathi *keḷ-* forms. Contraction and lateral/rhotic variation support this branch; the unrelated retroflex-d form *kaḍalī* is not selected. Updated disposition under the user’s explicit cross-Indo-Aryan policy: link this supported etymon despite unresolved inheritance versus intra-Indo-Aryan borrowing. The reflex edge records etymological family affiliation provisionally; it does not establish uninterrupted inheritance or an immediate donor. Prior hold: Banana kel-/ker- may be a contact form here (CDIAL explicitly labels Nepali kero a Maithili loan); donor pathway requires review.
